newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas stocks surge to close on foreign bids.
newsitem.headline: Caracas stocks surge to close on foreign bids.

text.p: Caracas stocks rallied to a strong close as foreign investors bid-up Venezuelan blue chips on renewed confidence in the economy and positive macroeconomic data, traders said.

"Inflation was much in line with market expectations ... Salary increases have been approved -- and they should not be too onerous or inflationary. And recent remarks by the IMF on Venezuela have had a tonic effect," said Banesco broker Simon Brad. The Central Bank reported April inflation at 2.4 percent, up from 1.6 percent in March but towards the bottom of the market's 2.1 to 3.0 percent forecast.

The market's 19-share index rallied just over two percent to close at 6,365.45 points as 22 million shares traded, worth 5.8 billion bolivars ($12 million) -- high volume compared with recent sessions
Merinvest's composite index, which includes telephone company CANTV, meanwhile rose 3.05 percent to end at 99.53 points.
"Foreign investors are returning to Venezuela ... they see the economy improving," said one broker, adding that most of their interest was still focused on the market's most liquid, blue chip stocks.

Among widely traded issues, CANTV closed up 133.00 bolivars at 2190.00; utility Electricidad de Caracas gained 9.50 bolivars to end at 531.50; and foods company Mavesa rose 7.50 bolivars to close at 87.25.
A total of 28 stocks rose, three fell and eight ended flat.
